title: After the midterms, AI has to find somewhere else to live (Thu 19 Nov off day, option fortytoone, approved by Krish 17 Nov)
experiment: One running stadium scoreboard (the infographic style Krish saved for this idea) carries the whole deck: the cover is the scoreboard lit at night reading VOTERS 40, DATA CENTRES 1, and each body card adds the next sourced line to the same board; meant to make the swipe read as one story and every number land as a score.

five_whys.q: Why does the midterm result matter for AI?
five_whys.a: On 3 November, voters chose to limit new data centres in 40 of 41 local votes across 10 states (Ballotpedia, 6 Nov 2026).

five_whys.q: Why did voters turn data centres away?
five_whys.a: Many fear a giant data centre pushes up their power bill: of Americans whose bills rose, 43% call data centres a major reason (Pew, May 2026).

five_whys.q: Why does that change where AI gets built?
five_whys.a: Builders need sites towns will accept, so they bring their own power, use smaller sites beside spare power, or shrink AI onto your own devices.

five_whys.q: Why is that a trend and not one election?
five_whys.a: Cleanview counted 59 planned US data centres with their own power plants by mid-2026, and OpenAI promised on 5 Nov to pay the full power cost of campuses it runs.

five_whys.q: Why should a business leader care?
five_whys.a: Where your AI supplier builds decides its cost, its delays and whether it keeps its promises, so ask where its new computing is being built.

cards.headline: Voters turned away AI's data centres. Where does AI live now?
cards.line: A data centre is the giant warehouse of computers that runs AI.
cards.picture: Full-bleed night scene drawn in code: a stadium scoreboard glowing over an empty small-town field, the board reading VOTERS 40, DATA CENTRES 1 in big lamp digits; the headline sits below the board

cards.headline: Voters backed limits on new data centres in 40 out of 41 local votes, after rows over power bills.
cards.picture: Sourced chart on the scoreboard: a grid of 41 ballot squares, 40 lit in coral marked LIMIT and 1 plain, with 10 STATES and 3 NOV on the board's side panels

cards.headline: Voters fear a giant data centre will push up their own power bill.
cards.line: Of Americans whose bills rose, 43% call data centres a major reason.
cards.picture: Sourced chart on the scoreboard: one bar filled to 43% beside an electricity-bill icon, labelled 'say data centres are a major reason their bill rose'

cards.headline: To dodge the fights, builders now bring their own power plants, and some AI runs on phones instead.
cards.line: One tracker counts 59 planned US data centres building their own plants.
cards.picture: Sourced chart on the scoreboard in three panels: 59 (planned US data centres with their own power plant), a row of small sites beside a solar field, and a phone with a chip glowing inside it
cards.source: Cleanview, behind-the-meter data centres report, mid-2026; OpenAI national community compact, 5 Nov 2026

cards.headline: Ask the company selling you AI where its new computing gets built, and who pays for power.
cards.line: Where it is built decides its cost, its delays and its promises.
cards.picture: The scoreboard's last line turned into a two-question checklist: WHERE IS IT BUILT? WHO PAYS FOR POWER? each with a tick box

cards.headline: Where AI gets built now decides what AI costs you and where it runs.
cards.picture: The scoreboard dimmed after the game, its final line reading WHERE IT'S BUILT = WHAT IT COSTS

read_back.reader: Fresh reader G (claude -p, Haiku, headlines only, once, 18 Nov)

answers.what: Local voters are pushing back against new AI data centres.
answers.happened: Voters rejected or limited new data centres in 40 of 41 local votes, after arguments over power bills.
answers.why: People worry a huge data centre nearby will raise their electricity bills.
answers.so_what: AI's physical buildout is now a local political fight, and that can shape what AI costs and where it runs.
answers.do: Ask AI providers where their new computing is built and who pays for the power.
